export type LastSeenPositionUnavailable = UnresolvedIntel<
  'never_observed'
>;

export type LastSeenPositionKnown = ResolvedIntel<{
  readonly lastSeenPosition: GridCell;
}>;

export interface PerceivedTargetKnowledge {
  readonly kind: 'perceived';
  readonly placementStatus: 'placed';
  readonly targetId: CombatantId;
  /** Current position is exposed only when the actor can mechanically locate it. */
  readonly position: GridCell;
  readonly effectiveSize: KnownCreatureSize;
  readonly placementMode: SerializedPlacementMode;
  readonly footprint: readonly [GridCell, ...GridCell[]];
  /** Nearest occupied-cell separation from the observing actor. */
  readonly distanceFeet: number;
  /** Positive markers only: an omitted condition is not asserted absent. */
  readonly conditions: readonly PerceivedConditionMarker[];
  readonly armorClass: ProjectedArmorClassKnowledge;
  readonly hitPoints: ProjectedHitPointKnowledge;
  readonly reciprocalVisibility: ProjectedReciprocalVisibility;
  readonly reaction: ProjectedReactionKnowledge;
}

/** A known last-seen position is not a current position. M7 has no source for one yet. */
export interface SuspectedTargetKnowledge {
  readonly kind: 'suspected';
  readonly targetId: CombatantId;
  readonly lastSeen: LastSeenPositionKnown;
}

export interface UnknownTargetKnowledge {
  readonly kind: 'unknown';
  readonly targetId: CombatantId;
  /** No observation-memory state exists from which a suspicion can be derived. */
  readonly lastSeen: LastSeenPositionUnavailable;
}

export interface PlacementPendingTargetKnowledge {
  readonly kind: 'placement_pending';
  readonly placementStatus: 'placement_pending';
  readonly targetId: CombatantId;
  readonly pendingReason: EncounterState['adjudicationPending'][number]['kind'];
}

/**
 * This shape intentionally contains no hidden/fog fields or reason codes.
 * It is the actor-facing knowledge projection, not a serialization of state.
 */
export type ActorTargetKnowledge =
  | PerceivedTargetKnowledge
  | SuspectedTargetKnowledge
  | UnknownTargetKnowledge
  | PlacementPendingTargetKnowledge;

export interface ActorKnowledgeProjection {
  readonly policy: ActorKnowledgePolicy;
  readonly actorId: CombatantId;
  readonly targets: readonly ActorTargetKnowledge[];
}

function unlocatedTarget(
  state: EncounterState,
  observer: CombatantId,
  targetId: CombatantId,
): SuspectedTargetKnowledge | UnknownTargetKnowledge {
  const observation = state.observationHistory.find((entry) =>
    entry.observer === observer && entry.subject === targetId);
  if (observation !== undefined) {
    return {
      kind: 'suspected',
      targetId,
      lastSeen: {
        status: 'resolved',
        lastSeenPosition: { ...observation.cell },
      },
    };
  }
  return {
    kind: 'unknown',
    targetId,
    lastSeen: {
      status: 'unresolved',
      reason: 'never_observed',
    },
  };
}

function isPerceivedConditionName(name: ConditionName): name is PerceivedConditionName {
  switch (name) {
    case 'Blinded':
    case 'Grappled':
    case 'Paralyzed':
    case 'Petrified':
}

/**
 * Projects living opponents as one actor can currently locate them, falling
 * back only to reducer-owned observation history.
 */
export function projectActorKnowledge(
  state: EncounterState,
  actorId: CombatantId,
): ActorKnowledgeProjection {
  if (!state.combatants.some((combatant) => combatant.profile.id === actorId)) {
    throw new RangeError(`Actor knowledge requires a combatant in this encounter: ${String(actorId)}.`);
  }
  const tokens = new Map(state.tokens.map((token) => [token.combatantId, token] as const));
  const actorIsPlaced = tokens.has(actorId) && !state.adjudicationPending.some((entry) =>
    entry.combatant === actorId);
  const targets = state.combatants
    .filter((candidate) => candidate.life !== 'dead' &&
      !combatantsAreAllies(state, actorId, candidate.profile.id))
    .map((candidate): ActorTargetKnowledge => {
      const targetId = candidate.profile.id;
      const target = tokens.get(targetId);
      const pending = state.adjudicationPending.find((entry) =>
        entry.combatant === targetId);
      if (pending !== undefined) {
        return {
          kind: 'placement_pending',
          placementStatus: 'placement_pending',
          targetId,
          pendingReason: pending.kind,
        };
      }
      if (target === undefined) {
        return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);
      }
      if (!actorIsPlaced) return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);

      const space = combatantSpace(state, targetId);
      const detection = detectCombatant(state, actorId, targetId);
      if (detection.kind === 'seen' || detection.kind === 'located') {
        const reciprocal = detectCombatant(state, targetId, actorId);
        const seen = detection.kind === 'seen';
        return {
          kind: 'perceived',
          placementStatus: 'placed',
          targetId,
          position: { ...target.position },
          effectiveSize: effectiveCreatureSize(state, targetId),
          placementMode: structuredClone(target.placementMode),
          footprint: space.cells.map((cell) => ({ ...cell })) as [GridCell, ...GridCell[]],
          distanceFeet: minimumSpaceDistance(combatantSpace(state, actorId), space),
          conditions: seen ? perceivedConditions(state, targetId) : [],
          armorClass: seen ? armorClassKnowledge(state, targetId) : { kind: 'unknown' },
          hitPoints: seen ? hitPointKnowledge(state, candidate) : { kind: 'unknown' },
          reciprocalVisibility: reciprocal.kind === 'seen'
            ? { kind: 'perceived', targetCanSeeActor: true }
            : { kind: 'unknown' },
          reaction: reactionKnowledge(state, targetId),
        };
      }
      return unlocatedTarget(state, actorId, targetId);
    })
    .sort((left, right) => String(left.targetId).localeCompare(String(right.targetId)));

  return {
    policy: ACTOR_KNOWLEDGE_POLICY,
    actorId,
    targets,
  };
}

/** Lets consumers name the versioned policy without accepting arbitrary strings. */
export function actorKnowledgePolicyVersion(): IntelPolicyVersion<'actor-knowledge-last-seen-v4'> {
  return ACTOR_KNOWLEDGE_POLICY;
}
}

export function canCombatantSee(
  state: EncounterState,
  observer: CombatantId,
  subject: CombatantId,
): boolean {
  return detectCombatant(state, observer, subject).kind === 'seen';
}

function observationKey(observer: CombatantId, subject: CombatantId): string {
  return `${String(observer)}\u0000${String(subject)}`;
}

/**
 * Refreshes only facts directly perceived in this state. An unperceived
 * subject's token is never read while retaining its earlier observation.
 */
export function reconcileObservationHistory(state: EncounterState): EncounterState {
  const hidden = new Set(state.hiddenCombatants.map((entry) => entry.combatant));
  const tokens = new Map(state.tokens.map((token) => [token.combatantId, token] as const));
  const presentCombatants = new Set(state.combatants.map((combatant) => combatant.profile.id));
  const presentLiving = new Set(state.combatants.flatMap((combatant) =>
    combatant.life !== 'dead' && tokens.has(combatant.profile.id)
      ? [combatant.profile.id]
      : []));
  const byPair = new Map(state.observationHistory
    .filter((entry) => presentCombatants.has(entry.observer) && presentLiving.has(entry.subject))
    .map((entry) => [observationKey(entry.observer, entry.subject), entry] as const));
  const validSpaces = new Map<CombatantId, ReturnType<typeof combatantSpace>>();
  for (const id of presentLiving) {
    try {
      validSpaces.set(id, combatantSpace(state, id));
    } catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof CreatureSizeRuleError)) throw error;
    }
  }
  const combatantIds = [...validSpaces.keys()].sort((left, right) => String(left).localeCompare(String(right)));
  for (const observer of combatantIds) {
    for (const subject of combatantIds) {
      if (observer === subject || hidden.has(subject) || !canCombatantSee(state, observer, subject)) continue;
      const token = tokens.get(subject);
      if (token === undefined) continue;
      const subjectSpace = validSpaces.get(subject);
      if (subjectSpace === undefined) continue;
      byPair.set(observationKey(observer, subject), {
        observer,
        subject,
        cell: { ...token.position },
        round: state.round,
        revision: state.revision,
      });
    }
  }
  return {
    ...state,
    observationHistory: [...byPair.values()].sort((left, right) =>
      String(left.observer).localeCompare(String(right.observer)) ||
      String(left.subject).localeCompare(String(right.subject))),
  };
}

  readonly observer: CombatantId;
  readonly target: CombatantId;
  readonly seen: boolean;
  readonly targetPosition: GridCell;
}

function monsterVisibilitySnapshot(state: EncounterState): readonly MonsterVisibilitySnapshot[] {
  const observers = state.combatants

function searchMemoryCause(
  state: EncounterState,
  observer: CombatantId,
  result: DetectionResult,
): SearchMemoryCause | null {
  if (result.kind !== 'undetected') return null;
  if (combatantConditions(state, observer).some((condition) => condition.name === 'Blinded')) {
    return null;
  }
  switch (result.reason) {
    case 'hidden': return 'hiding';
    case 'invisible': return 'invisibility';
    case 'obscured':
    case 'darkness':
      return 'obscurement';
    case 'blocked':
    case 'out_of_range':
      return null;
  }
}

function reconcileSearchMemories(
  context: ReductionContext,
  before: readonly MonsterVisibilitySnapshot[],
  command: EncounterCommand,
): void {
  const beforeByPair = new Map(before.map((entry) =>
    [`${String(entry.observer)}\u0000${String(entry.target)}`, entry] as const));
  for (const current of monsterVisibilitySnapshot(context.state)) {
    const prior = beforeByPair.get(`${String(current.observer)}\u0000${String(current.target)}`);
    const existing = encounterSearchMemories(context.state).find((memory) =>
      memory.observer === current.observer && memory.target === current.target);
    if (current.seen) {
      if (existing === undefined) continue;
      context.state = {
        ...context.state,
        searchMemories: encounterSearchMemories(context.state).filter((memory) => memory !== existing),
      };
      emit(context, {
        type: 'search_memory_cleared',
        visibility: 'dm_only',
        observer: existing.observer,
        target: existing.target,
        reason: 'target_reacquired',
      });
      continue;
    }
    const hiddenNow = command.type === 'hide' && command.actor === current.target &&
      context.events.some((event) =>
        event.type === 'hide_resolved' &&
        event.combatant === current.target &&
        event.outcome === 'hidden');
    if (prior?.seen !== true && !hiddenNow) continue;
    const cause = hiddenNow
      ? 'hiding' as const
      : searchMemoryCause(
          context.state,
          current.observer,
          detectCombatant(context.state, current.observer, current.target),
        );
    if (cause === null) continue;
    const memory = createSearchMemory({
      bounds: context.state.bounds,
      observer: current.observer,
      target: current.target,
      cause,
      lastKnownPosition: prior?.targetPosition ?? current.targetPosition,
      round: context.state.round,
    });
    context.state = {
      ...context.state,
      searchMemories: [
        ...encounterSearchMemories(context.state).filter((candidate) =>
          candidate.observer !== current.observer || candidate.target !== current.target),
        memory,
      ],
    };

function processSearch(
  context: ReductionContext,
  command: Extract<EncounterCommand, { readonly type: 'search' }>,
): void {
  assertActiveActor(context, command.actor);
  assertCanUseActions(context, command.actor);
  spendAction(context, command.actor, 'Search');
  const hidden = context.state.hiddenCombatants.find((entry) => entry.combatant === command.target);
  if (hidden === undefined) {
    emit(context, {
      type: 'search_resolved', combatant: command.actor, target: command.target,
      total: 0, outcome: 'target_not_hidden',
    });
    return;
  }
  const mode = perceptionMode(context.state, command.actor, command.target, command.reliance);
  if (mode === null) {
    emit(context, {
      type: 'search_resolved', combatant: command.actor, target: command.target,
      total: 0, outcome: 'not_found',
    });
    return;
  }
  const roll = rollD20(
    context.rng,
    mode,
    {
      kind: 'ability_check',
      source: `search:${command.reliance}`,
      actor: command.actor,
      target: command.target,
    },
  );
  const total = roll.chosen + (effectiveCombatRules(context.state, command.actor).skillBonuses?.perception ?? 0);
  const found = total >= hidden.stealthTotal;
  emit(context, {
    type: 'search_resolved', combatant: command.actor, target: command.target,
    total, outcome: found ? 'found' : 'not_found',
  });
  if (found) endHidden(context, command.target, 'found', command.actor);
}

function reactionPolicyFor(
  state: EncounterState,
  combatantId: CombatantId,
  reactionKind: DecisionPolicyKind,
): ReactionPolicy {
  return state.reactionPolicies.find((entry) =>
    entry.combatant === combatantId && entry.reactionKind === reactionKind)?.policy ?? 'ask';
}

function defaultOpportunityAttack(
  actor: CombatantId,
  target: CombatantId,
): Extract<EncounterCommand, { readonly type: 'opportunity_attack' }> {
  return {
    type: 'opportunity_attack', actor, target, attackBonus: 0, criticalFloor: 20,
    rollMode: 'normal', attackerCanSeeTarget: true, targetCanSeeAttacker: true,
      legalOptions: memory.legalOptions,
    });
  }
}

function advanceSearchMemories(context: ReductionContext): void {
  for (const memory of [...encounterSearchMemories(context.state)]) {
    if (context.state.round >= memory.expires.round) {
      context.state = {
        ...context.state,
        searchMemories: encounterSearchMemories(context.state).filter((candidate) => candidate !== memory),
      };
      emit(context, {
        type: 'search_memory_cleared',
        visibility: 'dm_only',
        observer: memory.observer,
        target: memory.target,
        reason: 'expired',
      });
      continue;
    }
    const expanded = expandSearchMemory(context.state.bounds, memory, context.state.round);
    if (expanded === memory) continue;
    context.state = {
      ...context.state,
      searchMemories: encounterSearchMemories(context.state).map((candidate) =>
        candidate === memory ? expanded : candidate),
    };
    emit(context, {
      type: 'suspicion_region_expanded',
      visibility: 'dm_only',
      observer: expanded.observer,
      target: expanded.target,
      suspicion: expanded.suspicion,
      expires: expanded.expires,
    });
  }
}

type PlanningRollDefenseEffect = EncounterEffect & {
  readonly payload: Extract<EffectPayload, { readonly kind: 'roll_defense_modifier' }>;
};

function isPlanningRollDefenseEffect(effect: EncounterEffect): effect is PlanningRollDefenseEffect {
  return effect.payload.kind === 'roll_defense_modifier';
}

   262	function executableCaster(room: GeneratedRoom): boolean {
   263	  return room.spec.monsterRoster.some((entry) => {
   264	    const row = BUNDLED_MONSTER_ROSTER.find((candidate) => candidate.id === entry.statblockId);
   265	    const actions = row?.statblock.sourceDetails.actions;
   266	    return actions?.kind === 'present' && actions.value.some((action) =>
   267	      action.kind === 'spellcasting' && action.execution?.kind !== 'absent' &&
   268	      action.spells.some((spell) => spell.manifestStatus === 'implemented'));
   269	  });
   270	}
   271	
   272	function everyMonsterProductive(room: GeneratedRoom): boolean {
   273	  const planningState = freshMonsterPlanningState(room.encounter.state);
   274	  return planningState.combatants
   275	    .filter((combatant) => combatant.profile.kind === 'monster')
   276	    .every((monster) => availableEngineActorOptions(planningState, monster.profile.id, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT)
   277	      .some((option) => {
   278	        const resolution = resolveEngineActorOption(planningState, option, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT);
   279	        return resolution.valid && (resolution.mechanics.movementCostFeet > 0 ||
   280	          resolution.mechanics.actionSlots.some((slot) =>
   281	            slot.kind === 'attack' || slot.kind === 'saving_throw' || slot.kind === 'cast_spell' ||
   282	            slot.kind === 'use_world_object'));
   283	      }));
   284	}

   286	/** State-derived brutal membership; hashes and creature names alone cannot satisfy it. */
   287	export function brutalRoomMembershipViolations(
   288	  room: GeneratedRoom,
   289	  sameSeedHard: GeneratedRoom = generateRoom(room.spec.seed, { difficulty: 'hard' }),
   290	): readonly D569SecondFamilyViolation[] {
   291	  const violations: D569SecondFamilyViolation[] = [];
   292	  addViolation(violations, room.spec.difficultyProfile === 'brutal', 'brutal_difficulty', 'room is not tagged brutal');
   293	  addViolation(
   294	    violations,
   295	    room.spec.challengeBudgetEighths ===
   296	      sameSeedHard.spec.challengeBudgetEighths * BRUTAL_CHALLENGE_BUDGET_SCALE &&
   297	      room.spec.challengeSpentEighths >= room.spec.challengeBudgetEighths * 0.9 &&
   298	      room.spec.challengeSpentEighths <= room.spec.challengeBudgetEighths,
   299	    'brutal_budget',
   300	    'brutal budget must be scaled from hard and spend 90-100 percent',
   301	  );
   302	  addViolation(
   303	    violations,
   304	    executableCaster(room),
   305	    'brutal_caster',
   306	    'brutal roster must contain an executable implemented caster',
   307	  );
   308	
   309	  const terrainCounts = {
   310	    difficult: room.spec.terrain.filter((feature) => feature.kind === 'difficult-terrain-patch').length,
   311	    hazards: room.spec.terrain.filter((feature) => feature.kind === 'hazard-object').length,
   312	    lights: room.spec.terrain.filter((feature) => feature.kind === 'light-source').length,
   313	    obscurement: room.spec.terrain.filter((feature) => feature.kind === 'obscurement-patch').length,
   314	  };
   315	  const terrainTotal = Object.values(terrainCounts).reduce((total, count) => total + count, 0);
   316	  addViolation(
   317	    violations,
   318	    terrainCounts.difficult >= 3 && terrainCounts.hazards >= 3 && terrainCounts.lights >= 2 &&
   319	      terrainCounts.obscurement >= 2 &&
   320	      terrainTotal >= BRUTAL_TERRAIN_FEATURE_COUNT_BAND.minimum &&
   321	      terrainTotal <= BRUTAL_TERRAIN_FEATURE_COUNT_BAND.maximum &&
   322	      room.spec.terrain.length > sameSeedHard.spec.terrain.length,
   323	    'brutal_terrain',
   324	    'brutal terrain must meet every configured minimum/count band and exceed hard density',
   325	  );
   326	  addViolation(
   327	    violations,
   328	    everyMonsterProductive(room),
   329	    'brutal_productivity',
   330	    'every brutal monster must have a productive first-turn offer',
   331	  );
   332	  return violations;
   333	}

158:export function terrainWallCells(state: TerrainState): readonly GridCell[] {
/** Passability remains independent from cover tracing during the 1a/1b wire seam. */
export function terrainPassabilityOfWireBlocking(
  blocking: WorldObjectBlockingWire,
): TerrainPassability {
  if (blocking.movement) return 'blocked';
  switch (blocking.cover) {
    case 'none': return 'open';
    case 'half': return 'difficult';
    case 'three_quarters': return 'blocked';
    case 'total': return 'blocked';
  }
}

export function terrainWallCells(state: TerrainState): readonly GridCell[] {
  const cells = [
    ...state.blockedCells,
    ...state.worldObjects.flatMap((object) =>
      terrainKindOfWireBlocking(object.blocking) === 'wall' ? object.footprint : []),
  ];
  return [...new Map(cells.map((cell) => [cellKey(cell), cell] as const)).values()];
}

/** Runtime interpretation during the 1a/1b atomic seam; cover is the stable wire discriminant. */
export function terrainKindOfWireBlocking(blocking: WorldObjectBlockingWire): TerrainKind {
  switch (blocking.cover) {
    case 'none': return 'open';
    case 'half': return 'half_cover';
    case 'three_quarters': return 'three_quarters_cover';
    case 'total': return 'wall';
  }
}

function useTargets(
  state: EncounterState,
  actorId: CombatantId,
  use: EngineMainActionUse | EngineBonusActionUse,
  queries: EngineQueryPort,
): readonly CombatantId[] | null {
  switch (use.kind) {
    case 'attack': {
      const resolved = targetUse(state, actorId, use, queries);
      return resolved === null ? null : [resolved.targetId];
    }
    case 'multiattack': {
      const targets = use.components.map((component) => component.kind === 'attack'
        ? targetUse(state, actorId, component, queries)
        : savingThrowTargetUse(state, actorId, component, queries));
      return targets.some((entry) => entry === null)
        ? null
        : targets.flatMap((entry) => entry === null ? [] : [entry.targetId]);
    }
    case 'saving_throw': {
      const targetId = resolveSelector(state, actorId, use.target, queries);
      return targetId === null ? null : [targetId];
    }
    case 'cast_spell': {
      const targets = use.targets.map((selector) => resolveSelector(state, actorId, selector, queries));
      return targets.some((targetId) => targetId === null)
        ? null
        : targets.flatMap((targetId) => targetId === null ? [] : [targetId]);
    }
    case 'use_world_object':
    case 'dodge':
    case 'disengage':
    case 'dash':
    case 'hide':
    case 'end_turn': return [];
  }
}

+# BLIND-01 implementation plan
+
+Date: 2026-09-18  
+Planning base: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01`, branch
+`claude/blind-01`, commit `b94dd73221697e3d03da8991746726563777fa74`.  
+Authoritative decisions: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-multiclass-spells-static/.claude/decisions.md`
+D420, D476, D545, D617, D625, D632, D636.6, D641-D643, and D662-D664.
+All paths below are relative to `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01` unless an
+absolute path is printed.
+
+## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
+
+Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
+none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
+has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
+open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
+Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.
+
+Hard invariants:
+
+- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
+- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
+  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
+- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
+  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
+- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
+  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
+- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
+  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
+  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
+- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.
+
+Sequencing/ownership:
+
+1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
+   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.
+2. COHORT-01 then creates/lands its already-authorized v2/v6 code surface; apply B5-B6 against that
+   rebased tip. This is not permission to alter v1/v5 rows or any fixture bytes.
+3. `src/vtt/intent-resolver.ts`, `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts`, and
+   `src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts` are also owned by ELEVATION-02's 221-path manifest (D636.6) and the
+   D584 72-path inventory. The supervisor must record: `BLIND-01 landed first; ELEVATION_BASE_REV
+   includes BLIND-01; ELEVATION-02 must rebase, retain pursue_indication/seek_cover/search and the
+   cover query, and rerun both ownership overlays before B0.` A conflict may not silently drop them.
+
+## 2. Knowledge branching
+
+Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
+`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
+
+Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
+`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
+`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
+
+| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
+|---|---|---|
+| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
+| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
+| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
+| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
+| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
+| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
+
+Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
+party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
+active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
+Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
+row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
+
+Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
+
+- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
+  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
+  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
+- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
+  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
+  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
+  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
+- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
+  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
+  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
+  standard offers should expose them at all.
+
+## 3. Topology-only cover objective
+
+### 3.1 Open approaches
+
+Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
+implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
+
+1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
+   `blocked`.
+2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
+   `blocking.movement === false`.
+3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
+   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
+   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
+   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
+
+Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
+approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
+
+### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
+
+Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
+`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
+`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
+approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
+
+- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
+  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
+  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
+  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
+- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
+  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
+  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
+- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
+  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
+  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
+  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
+  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
+- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
+  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
+  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
+
+### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
+
+Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
+at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
+speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
+
+| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
+|---|---:|---|---|
+| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 5-10 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| reachable rows 1 and 3 | independently path-checked | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+
+Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
+against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
+obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
+half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.
+
+## 4. Offer and execution shape
+
+Make `EngineEngagement` at `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts:109-123` a discriminated union with:
+
+- existing target stances unchanged;
+- `{stance:'pursue_indication', indication: KnownIndication}` where the typed indication contains
+  only observation/search-memory knowledge and never a current unseen position; and
+- `{stance:'seek_cover', objective:{kind:'open_approach_cover', policy:'blind-cover-v1'}}`, with no
+  anchor, target, cell, or selector.
+
+Add main action `{kind:'search', targetId, reliance:'sight'}` and resolved `search` to the closed
+action unions. The offer/executor flow is:
+
+- Pursuit: normal-speed movement objective + main Search. Resolve the indicated region through
+  injected queries, move, then execute the existing Search reducer command.
+- Blind posture: normal-speed `seek_cover` objective + main Dodge, label `Seek Cover + Dodge`.
+  `engine-round-session.ts:248-315` already applies movement before action. This is not Dash+Dodge:
+  Dash and Dodge both consume the one main slot; Dash is not emitted for the posture.
+
+Update every exhaustive switch. Search is utility, not offense/damage; it is productive only as the
+typed pursuit. `basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes
+`pursue_indication` and `seek_cover` as advance options before its defense fallback; ordinary offense
+still wins. The existing Dash declaration (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`) remains only in the normal
+branch. Keep the current action-slot/resource validations.
+
+`engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body (`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`), so new
+objectives intentionally change IDs for the new/replaced options; unchanged normal option bodies keep
+their IDs. Never pin an ID copied from post-change output: construct the expected body by hand and
+hash it with the independent canonical-json/SHA helper already used by the tests.
+
+No-coordinate witness: deep-walk the canonical blind-posture offer body and assert (a) no opponent
+CombatantId string occurs, (b) no GridCell-shaped `{column,row}` value occurs, and (c) movement has
+only the policy tag. A control pursuit offer contains its historical cell, proving the walker is live.
+Resolved mechanics may contain the chosen cover destination; the offer body may not. Leak the sealed
+PC's `(7,2)` into the objective for the required mutant and this witness must fail.
+
+## 5. Productivity contract
+
+Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
+`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
+`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
+A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
+
+1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
+2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
+3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
+
+An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
+one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
+monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
+action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.
+
+Frozen expected remeasurement, from the pre-change population (not changed output):

+| hard 5117 | 55 / 75 | 55 / 55 |

+| brutal-2 6207 | 29 / 44 | 29 / 29 |

+| aggregate | 185 / 251 | 185 / 185 |

+All 36 blind 6209 monsters and all 185 measured blind monsters are productive under the amended
+contract, even when a best-cover origin yields zero movement.

+# BLIND-01 implementation plan
+
+Date: 2026-09-18  
+Planning base: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01`, branch
+`claude/blind-01`, commit `b94dd73221697e3d03da8991746726563777fa74`.

+D420, D476, D545, D617, D625, D632, D636.6, D641-D643, and D662-D664.

+absolute path is printed.

+## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
+
+Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
+none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
+has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
+open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
+Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.
+
+Hard invariants:
+
+- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
+- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
+  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
+- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
+  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
+- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
+  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
+- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
+  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
+  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
+- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.
+
+Sequencing/ownership:
+
+1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
+   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.
+2. COHORT-01 then creates/lands its already-authorized v2/v6 code surface; apply B5-B6 against that
+   rebased tip. This is not permission to alter v1/v5 rows or any fixture bytes.
+3. `src/vtt/intent-resolver.ts`, `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts`, and
+   `src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts` are also owned by ELEVATION-02's 221-path manifest (D636.6) and the
+   D584 72-path inventory. The supervisor must record: `BLIND-01 landed first; ELEVATION_BASE_REV
+   includes BLIND-01; ELEVATION-02 must rebase, retain pursue_indication/seek_cover/search and the
+   cover query, and rerun both ownership overlays before B0.` A conflict may not silently drop them.

+## 2. Knowledge branching
+
+Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
+`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
+
+Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
+`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
+`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
+
+| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
+|---|---|---|
+| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
+| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
+| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
+| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
+| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
+| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
+
+Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
+party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
+active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
+Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
+row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
+
+Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
+
+- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
+  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
+  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
+- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
+  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
+  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
+  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
+- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
+  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
+  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
+  standard offers should expose them at all.

+## 3. Topology-only cover objective
+
+### 3.1 Open approaches
+
+Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
+implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
+
+1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
+   `blocked`.
+2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
+   `blocking.movement === false`.
+3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
+   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
+   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
+   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
+
+Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
+approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
+
+### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
+
+Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
+`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
+`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
+approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
+
+- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
+  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
+  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
+  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
+- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
+  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
+  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
+- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
+  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
+  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
+  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
+  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
+- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
+  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
+  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
+
+### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
+
+Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
+at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
+speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
+
+| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
+|---|---:|---|---|
+| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 5-10 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| reachable rows 1 and 3 | independently path-checked | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+
+Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
+against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
+obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
+half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.

+## 4. Offer and execution shape
+
+Make `EngineEngagement` at `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts:109-123` a discriminated union with:

+- existing target stances unchanged;
+- `{stance:'pursue_indication', indication: KnownIndication}` where the typed indication contains

+- `{stance:'seek_cover', objective:{kind:'open_approach_cover', policy:'blind-cover-v1'}}`, with no

+Add main action `{kind:'search', targetId, reliance:'sight'}` and resolved `search` to the closed
+action unions. The offer/executor flow is:
+
+- Pursuit: normal-speed movement objective + main Search. Resolve the indicated region through
+  injected queries, move, then execute the existing Search reducer command.
+- Blind posture: normal-speed `seek_cover` objective + main Dodge, label `Seek Cover + Dodge`.
+  `engine-round-session.ts:248-315` already applies movement before action. This is not Dash+Dodge:
+  Dash and Dodge both consume the one main slot; Dash is not emitted for the posture.

+Update every exhaustive switch. Search is utility, not offense/damage; it is productive only as the
+typed pursuit. `basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes
+`pursue_indication` and `seek_cover` as advance options before its defense fallback; ordinary offense
+still wins. The existing Dash declaration (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`) remains only in the normal

+`engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body (`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`), so new
+objectives intentionally change IDs for the new/replaced options; unchanged normal option bodies keep

+## 5. Productivity contract
+
+Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
+`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
+`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
+A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
+
+1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
+2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
+3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
+
+An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
+one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
+monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
+action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.

+

+## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
+
+Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
+none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
+has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
+open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
+Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.
+
+Hard invariants:
+
+- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
+- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
+  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
+- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
+  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
+- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
+  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
+- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
+  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
+  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
+- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.
+
+Sequencing/ownership:
+
+1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
+   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.

+## 2. Knowledge branching
+
+Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
+`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
+
+Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
+`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
+`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
+
+| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
+|---|---|---|
+| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
+| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
+| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
+| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
+| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
+| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
+
+Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
+party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
+active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
+Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
+row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
+
+Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
+
+- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
+  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
+  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
+- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
+  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
+  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
+  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
+- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
+  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
+  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
+  standard offers should expose them at all.

+## 3. Topology-only cover objective
+
+### 3.1 Open approaches
+
+Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
+implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
+
+1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
+   `blocked`.
+2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
+   `blocking.movement === false`.
+3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
+   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
+   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
+   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
+
+Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
+approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
+
+### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
+
+Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
+`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
+`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
+approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
+
+- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
+  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
+  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
+  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
+- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
+  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
+  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
+- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
+  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
+  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
+  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
+  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
+- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
+  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
+  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
+
+### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
+
+Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
+at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
+speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
+
+| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
+|---|---:|---|---|
+| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 5-10 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| reachable rows 1 and 3 | independently path-checked | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+
+Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
+against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
+obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
+half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.

+## 5. Productivity contract
+
+Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
+`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
+`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
+A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
+
+1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
+2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
+3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
+
+An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
+one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
+monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
+action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.

+## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
+Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
+none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
+has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
+open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
+Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.

+## 2. Knowledge branching
+Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
+`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
+
+Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
+`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
+`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
+
+| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
+|---|---|---|
+| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
+| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
+| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
+| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
+| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
+| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
+
+Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
+party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
+active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
+Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
+row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
+
+Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
+
+- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
+  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
+  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
+- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
+  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
+  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
+  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
+- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
+  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
+  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
+  standard offers should expose them at all.

+## 3. Topology-only cover objective
+
+### 3.1 Open approaches
+
+Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
+implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
+
+1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
+   `blocked`.
+2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
+   `blocking.movement === false`.
+3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
+   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
+   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
+   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
+
+Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
+approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
+
+### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
+
+Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
+`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
+`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
+approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
+
+- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
+  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
+  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
+  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
+- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
+  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
+  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
+- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
+  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
+  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
+  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
+  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
+- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
+  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
+  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
+
+### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
+
+Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
+at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
+speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
+
+| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
+|---|---:|---|---|
+| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 5-10 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| reachable rows 1 and 3 | independently path-checked | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+
+Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
+against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
+obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
+half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.
+
+## 4. Offer and execution shape
+
+Make `EngineEngagement` at `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts:109-123` a discriminated union with:

+- existing target stances unchanged;
+- `{stance:'pursue_indication', indication: KnownIndication}` where the typed indication contains

+- `{stance:'seek_cover', objective:{kind:'open_approach_cover', policy:'blind-cover-v1'}}`, with no

+action unions. The offer/executor flow is:
+
+- Pursuit: normal-speed movement objective + main Search. Resolve the indicated region through
+  injected queries, move, then execute the existing Search reducer command.
+- Blind posture: normal-speed `seek_cover` objective + main Dodge, label `Seek Cover + Dodge`.
+  `engine-round-session.ts:248-315` already applies movement before action. This is not Dash+Dodge:
+  Dash and Dodge both consume the one main slot; Dash is not emitted for the posture.

+Update every exhaustive switch. Search is utility, not offense/damage; it is productive only as the
+typed pursuit. `basic_advance` (`src/vtt/snippets/registry.ts:158-202`) recognizes
+`pursue_indication` and `seek_cover` as advance options before its defense fallback; ordinary offense
+still wins. The existing Dash declaration (`offer-declarations.ts:497-506`) remains only in the normal
+branch. Keep the current action-slot/resource validations.

+`engineOfferableOption` hashes the canonical offer body (`src/vtt/option-modeling.ts:26-33`), so new

+No-coordinate witness: deep-walk the canonical blind-posture offer body and assert (a) no opponent

+## 5. Productivity contract
+
+Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
+`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
+`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
+A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
+
+1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
+2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
+3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
+
+An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
+one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
+monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
+action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.
+

+All 36 blind 6209 monsters and all 185 measured blind monsters are productive under the amended

+# BLIND-01 implementation plan
+
+Date: 2026-09-18  
+Planning base: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01`, branch
+`claude/blind-01`, commit `b94dd73221697e3d03da8991746726563777fa74`.  
+Authoritative decisions: `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-multiclass-spells-static/.claude/decisions.md`
+D420, D476, D545, D617, D625, D632, D636.6, D641-D643, and D662-D664.
+All paths below are relative to `/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-blind-01` unless an
+absolute path is printed.
+
+## 1. Outcome, sequencing, and invariants
+Implement D664 exactly: when a monster perceives an enemy, retain normal offers; when it perceives
+none but has an actor-known directional indication, move and Search toward that indication; when it
+has no indication, move at normal speed to the best topology-only cover available against the room's
+open approaches and take Dodge. If its current cell is already tied for best reachable cover, take
+Dodge without moving. Both forms of the blind posture are productive.
+
+Hard invariants:
+- Never read an unperceived PC token, current position, distance, or route. D476/D545 remain intact.
+- `projectActorKnowledge` remains the single actor-knowledge producer (D625). Offer code must not
+  inspect `observationHistory` or `searchMemories` independently.
+- The resolver calls only its injected `environment.queries`; it must not import or construct the
+  canonical query port, movement world, terrain helpers, or cover tracer (D617.5).
+- No fixture byte changes. No expectation may be copied from changed-code output. Unchanged fields
+  may be carried from the pre-change `b94dd732` tree; every changed behavioral value is hand-derived.
+- `generateRoom` does not consult offers: `src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1426` and
+  `tools/generate-arena-basis.ts:251-345` have no offer/resolver/query-port import. All 42 currently
+  tracked generated rooms must remain byte-identical; BLIND-01 does not regenerate them.
+- No full Vitest, Playwright, build, browser server, or port 4173. Use only the targeted commands below.
+
+Sequencing/ownership:
+1. Implement B1-B4 on the stated base. Merge the accepted core into `claude/vis-field`, then into
+   `claude/cohort-01` before COHORT-01 Batch 3 re-runs, as D664 requires.
+2. COHORT-01 then creates/lands its already-authorized v2/v6 code surface; apply B5-B6 against that
+   rebased tip. This is not permission to alter v1/v5 rows or any fixture bytes.
+3. `src/vtt/intent-resolver.ts`, `src/vtt/turn-proposal.ts`, and
+   `src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts` are also owned by ELEVATION-02's 221-path manifest (D636.6) and the
+   D584 72-path inventory. The supervisor must record: `BLIND-01 landed first; ELEVATION_BASE_REV
+   includes BLIND-01; ELEVATION-02 must rebase, retain pursue_indication/seek_cover/search and the
+   cover query, and rerun both ownership overlays before B0.` A conflict may not silently drop them.
+
+## 2. Knowledge branching
+Current facts are at `src/vtt/intel/actor-knowledge.ts:42-90,98-123,226-289` and
+`src/combat/search-memory.ts:15-64,88-101,103-150`.
+
+Add a typed, internal `projectActorTurnKnowledge(state, actorId)` beside
+`projectActorKnowledge`. It first consumes that projection, then joins only active reducer-owned
+`SearchMemory` rows for the actor. It returns one closed union:
+
+| Knowledge outcome | Directional indication | Offer branch |
+|---|---|---|
+| At least one `perceived` target (`seen` or mechanically `located`) | Current actor-known position | `normal`; call the existing normal declaration path unchanged. Do not also emit blind/pursuit offers. |
+| No perceived target; active `SearchMemory` for a living opponent | Existing `lastKnownPosition`, `suspicion.cells`, and the existing `legalOptions` | `pursue_indication`; one option per memory containing `move_and_search`. |
+| No perceived target; `suspected` target with observation-history `lastSeenPosition`, but no memory for that pair | That historical singleton cell | `pursue_indication`; one option for the observation. |
+| `unknown` / `never_observed` | None | Contributes no cue. |
+| `placement_pending` | None | Contributes no cue; pending placement never exposes a position. |
+| No perceived targets and no cues after the preceding rows | None | `blind_posture` (`seek_cover` + Dodge). |
+
+Those are all cues defined today. There is no hearing marker, alert vector, nearest-enemy fallback,
+party centroid, initiative inference, or unseen-token cue; do not invent one. For the same target, an
+active memory supersedes its duplicate observation-history cue because it owns the expanding region.
+Sort independent cues by target id, source (`search_memory` before `observation_history`), then
+row/column; emit each rather than guessing which enemy matters.
+
+Reuse rather than duplicate D420 machinery:
+
+- For a memory, select its existing `legalOptions` member with `kind: 'move_and_search'`; carry that
+  typed member and its existing Search citation into the pursuit objective. Use the existing
+  `suspicion.cells` verbatim. Never recreate the region, radius, roll mode, or citations in offers.
+- The pursue destination minimizes distance to any indicated cell, then path cost, row, column,
+  using query-port results. It moves no farther than normal speed and then issues the existing
+  `{type:'search', actor, target, reliance:'sight'}` command (`src/combat/events.ts:95-100` and
+  `src/combat/encounter.ts:4820-4857`). Reaching the indication is not required in one turn.
+- Existing `attack_suspected_square` entries, their exact `cells`, forced Disadvantage, and reducer
+  command (`src/combat/events.ts:216-228`, `src/combat/encounter.ts:7457`) remain the sole machinery
+  for that escalation. BLIND-01 does not clone them into a second shape; Q2 below decides whether
+  standard offers should expose them at all.

+## 3. Topology-only cover objective
+
+### 3.1 Open approaches
+
+Compute the same stable row-major set for every candidate, entirely inside the canonical query-port
+implementation, from `bounds`, `blockedCells`, and `worldObjects`:
+
+1. **Unblocked frontier:** every in-bounds boundary cell whose effective terrain passability is not
+   `blocked`.
+2. **Open doorway:** every in-bounds/passable footprint cell of a world object with `kind:'door'` and
+   `blocking.movement === false`.
+3. **Wall-structure aperture:** every in-bounds/passable cell whose immediate north+south neighbors
+   are both in `terrainWallCells(state)`, or whose immediate west+east neighbors are both wall cells.
+   This is the exact one-cell aperture in an otherwise continuous cardinal wall; an out-of-bounds
+   neighbor does not count. Wider boundary openings are already frontier; authored doors are row 2.
+
+Deduplicate by `column,row` and sort row then column. Closed doors and blocked cells are not
+approaches. If the set is empty, every destination has the same empty profile and the origin wins.
+
+### 3.2 Candidates, score, and tie order
+
+Add one `EngineQueryPort` method, `seekCover(state, request)`, to
+`src/vtt/engine-query-port.ts:203-251`; the resolver only invokes
+`environment.queries.seekCover`. Its result contains the selected legal path/cost/destination plus
+approaches and score evidence for tests. Inside the canonical port:
+
+- Candidate anchors are the origin plus every in-bounds anchor for which the actor's full footprint
+  fits and the existing canonical `path` query returns legal under `movement:'normal'` and
+  `maximumFeet <= current speed`. The returned path and cost are used; no second movement world or
+  geometric reach approximation is allowed (`engine-query-port.ts:1060-1131`).
+- For each `(destination, approach)`, call existing `traceTerrainLine` (`src/combat/cover.ts:795-802`).
+  It includes `blockedCells`, world objects, the physical tier kernel also exposed by
+  `coverTierBetweenObjects` (`cover.ts:870-913`), and D635/D642/D657 optical solid-wall rules.
+- Encode one approach strength as `[blocksSight ? 1 : 0, coverRank(tier)]`, with ranks
+  none=0, half=1, three-quarters=2, total=3. Sort a destination's strengths weakest-first. Compare
+  equal-length vectors lexicographically, largest value winning: maximize the worst protected open
+  approach, then the next-worst, and so on. This makes an optically sealed line stronger than a
+  visible line at the same/lower physical tier; Q1 is the only alternative.
+- Select the maximum profile. If origin has that profile, select origin (movement 0). Otherwise use
+  lowest actual path cost, then lower row, then lower column. Thus a merely equal cell never causes
+  motion, while a strictly better cell does.
+
+### 3.3 Hand oracle used before implementation
+
+Use a 9x5 scene: outer perimeter blocked except `(0,2)`; a full-height wall at column 6 seals a PC
+at `(7,2)` from the monster; a passable half-cover object occupies `(2,2)`; monster starts `(1,2)`,
+speed 30; no history/memory. The only open approach is `(0,2)`.
+
+| Destination group | Canonical path cost | Trace from `(0,2)` | Profile |
+|---|---:|---|---|
+| origin `(1,2)` and `(2,2)` | 0 / 5-10 | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+| `(3,2)` | 10 via an open diagonal around `(2,2)` | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| `(4,2)`, `(5,2)` | 15, 20 | half, sight clear | `[(0,1)]` |
+| reachable rows 1 and 3 | independently path-checked | none, sight clear | `[(0,0)]` |
+
+Therefore choose `(3,2)`, then Dodge. The query-port test must first verify every table trace directly
+against `traceTerrainLine` and the half-cover object against `coverTierBetweenObjects`; it may not
+obtain this expectation from `seekCover`. With the monster starting at `(3,2)`, origin ties the other
+half-cover cells and must win at cost 0, followed by Dodge. This is the sealed-wall RED pair.

+## 5. Productivity contract
+
+Replace the duplicated predicate with one exported structural helper owned by
+`tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:272-283`; the active v2 suite at
+`tests/unit/vtt/arena-basis-brutal-v2.test.ts:77-104` and the brutal-b membership test call it.
+A valid option is productive iff at least one holds:
+
+1. existing positive movement, attack, saving throw, cast, or world-object action;
+2. main Search paired with `pursue_indication` (movement may be 0 if already in the region); or
+3. exactly one main Dodge paired with `seek_cover`, whether movement is positive or 0.
+
+An arbitrary stationary Dodge remains unproductive. A room is unproductive precisely when at least
+one living monster has no valid option in any of those three classes. Consequently a no-indication
+monster already at best cover is productive; inability to improve cover is not failure. An unplaced,
+action-spent, or otherwise invalid actor remains unproductive if no posture resolves.
